spec_text:
Task: write a Python function solve(n) that returns how many prime numbers are strictly smaller than n. The argument n is an integer with 0 <= n <= 50000. A prime number is an integer greater than 1 whose only positive divisors are 1 and itself, so for n = 10 the answer is 4 (2, 3, 5 and 7), and for n = 0, 1 or 2 the answer is 0.

Use only the Python standard library. Return only one ```python code block containing the function solve and any helpers, with no example usage and no explanation.

catalogue.mechanism: mark the multiples of every prime in a boolean array of size n (slice assignment or inner loops) and count the unmarked entries
test each number for divisibility by smaller numbers (all integers, 6k +- 1 candidates or the primes found so far) up to its square root
keep a list of primes and cross off i * p for primes p up to the smallest prime factor of i, breaking when p divides i, so each composite is crossed once
sieve the range in fixed-size blocks using the primes up to the square root of n
cross out i + j + 2ij for 1 <= i <= j and map each surviving k to the odd prime 2k + 1
toggle candidates by the quadratic forms 4x^2 + y^2, 3x^2 + y^2 and 3x^2 - y^2 modulo 12, then remove multiples of squares of primes
